Question #1
```{r}
respond <- 1:20
sex <- c(2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2)
f_occ <- c(1, 3, 3, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 1, 3, 2, 1, 3, 3, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1)
p_home <- c(5, 7, 3, 8, 5, 9, 6, 7, 8, 4, 7, 5, 4, 7, 8, 8, 3, 11, 7, 6)
s_school <- c(6, 4, 4, 1, 2, 1, 5, 3, 1, 2, 3, 2, 5, 5, 2, 1, 2, 5, 3, 2)
h_type <- c(1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 3, 3, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2)

c(length(respond),length(sex),length(f_occ),length(p_home),length(s_school),length(h_type))
```
```{r}
results <- data.frame(
  Respond  = respond,
  Sex      = sex,
  FathersOccupation    = f_occ,
  PersonAtHome   = p_home,
  SiblingAtSchool = s_school,
  TypeofHouses   = h_type
)

results
```
```{r}
#a.
str(results)
summary(results)


#b.
dim(results)
nrow(results)
ncol(results)


#c.
sex <- factor (sex,
        levels = c(1, 2),
        labels = c("Male", "Female"))

f_occ <- factor (f_occ,
        levels = c(1, 2, 3),
        labels = c("Farmer", "Driver","Others"))

h_type <- factor (h_type,
        levels = c(1, 2, 3),
        labels = c("Wood", "Semi-COncrete","COncrete"))
table(sex)
table(f_occ)
table(h_type)

#d.
colMeans(results)
```
```{r}

results[1:5,]

types_houses
```

Question #3
```{r}
#Sex, FathersOccupation, and TypesOfHouses are categories (nominal data), because the numbers are 
#only codes for groups. PersonsAtHome and SiblingsAtSchool are real counts. Averaging Sex won't make #sense since it's only a category, so the Mean won't describe anything.
```
